builder_plan.scenario: A product assistant retrieves plausible documents but gives unsupported answers.
builder_plan.change: Change one retrieval or ranking step while keeping the document snapshot fixed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retrieval pipeline with identical questions and answer model.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Supported answers, retrieval misses, correct abstentions, index cost, and response latency.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Signed but Steerable: Measuring and Closing the Text-Vector Integrity Gap in Offline Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: The method replaces trusting signatures plus cosine-tolerance recomputation of precomputed embeddings in offline RAG knowledge packs with verifier-controlled recomputation, quantisation-code verification, guard bands, and canonicalisation. It costs verifier-side embedding recomputation per update and added pipeline complexity for cross-platform canonicalisation, since common FP32 and dynamic-INT8 pipelines are not bit-reproducible across batch sizes and architectures. It can fail where deployment pipelines cannot be made deterministic enough to set a valid guard band, and abstention, context pruning, and semantic screening showed pre-registered negative results as alternative defences.
rationale: The threat model applies only to teams shipping offline or edge RAG updated via third-party signed packs with precomputed vectors, so the reader should adopt the code-verification pattern only if that architecture matches their production system.
technique: Verifier-recomputed embedding integrity checks for signed RAG packs

claims.statement: The method replaces trusting signatures plus cosine-tolerance recomputation of precomputed embeddings in offline RAG knowledge packs with verifier-controlled recomputation, quantisation-code verification, guard bands, and canonicalisation. It costs verifier-side embedding recomputation per update and added pipeline complexity for cross-platform canonicalisation, since common FP32 and dynamic-INT8 pipelines are not bit-reproducible across batch sizes and architectures. It can fail where deployment pipelines cannot be made deterministic enough to set a valid guard band, and abstention, context pruning, and semantic screening showed pre-registered negative results as alternative defences.

Unverified signed packs leave up to 5.5% of queries hijackable at floating-point-noise tolerance (98-100% at an INT8-calibrated tolerance); on a Raspberry Pi 5 the attack drops correct answers from 0.75 to 0.39, and 25% of targets are hijacked past a product-quantisation audit, while the proposed code-verification guard accepted all honest vectors and blocked tampering.
